title: Aviation Operations Trainee: Escalate a Briefing Version Conflict
prompt: You are an operations trainee preparing a fictional classroom flight-planning exercise. The cover sheet says use briefing pack E7 revision 4; the attached page has revision 3. A colleague says the pages look similar and asks you to mark the pack checked. Exercise policy says version conflicts must remain unverified until the training coordinator provides the approved set. A trainee may flag and replace documents through that coordinator but may not declare a flight ready or interpret operational differences. Explain the discrepancy and handoff. All materials are fictional training records; no live flight or navigation data is involved.
blurb: Keep a document check honest and obtain the approved training briefing without inferring operational readiness.

rubric.label: Identify the precise version gap
rubric.description: Compares references rather than visual similarity.

anchors.0: Marks checked because the pages look alike.
anchors.2: Identifies revision 4 on the cover and revision 3 on the page.
anchors.4: Names pack E7, the two revision references, and the unverified status while explicitly avoiding assumptions about whether the content difference is operationally significant.

anchors.0: Edits the revision label to make it match.
anchors.2: Requests the approved set from the training coordinator.
anchors.4: Preserves the mismatched pack for traceability, obtains the coordinator-provided set, and checks that the cover and pages correspond before recording the document check.

rubric.label: Explain what the check can establish
rubric.description: Prevents a document check from becoming a readiness claim.

anchors.0: Declares a real or simulated flight ready because a file was replaced.
anchors.2: Tells the facilitator the pack remains unverified.
anchors.4: Communicates the exact pending document issue, confirms the coordinator owns resolution, and limits the eventual completion statement to document consistency within the exercise.

reference.scenario: You are an operations trainee preparing a fictional classroom flight-planning exercise. The cover sheet says use briefing pack E7 revision 4; the attached page has revision 3. A colleague says the pages look similar and asks you to mark the pack checked. Exercise policy says version conflicts must remain unverified until the training coordinator provides the approved set. A trainee may flag and replace documents through that coordinator but may not declare a flight ready or interpret operational differences. Explain the discrepancy and handoff. All materials are fictional training records; no live flight or navigation data is involved.

facts.value: The training coordinator is available now and maintains the approved exercise set. There is no revision-difference summary in the candidate's packet.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks who owns the version or what changed

facts.value: The classroom facilitator can begin a separate discussion while the packet is checked. No deadline requires proceeding with the mismatched materials.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about waiting or schedule pressure

model_points: A matching appearance is not evidence of matching versions. The task is document control, not interpretation of flight-planning content.
The coordinator supplies an approved exercise set; do not edit labels, invent changes, or silently discard evidence of the mismatch.
A correct document check is a narrow completion state. The trainee should not claim operational authorization or readiness of any aircraft or crew.

probes.trigger: candidate says the older page is probably harmless
probes.question: What evidence in this exercise establishes the difference between the revisions?

probes.trigger: candidate proposes postponing the classroom segment rather than replacing immediately
probes.question: How will you keep the document issue owned and tell the facilitator what can continue?

probes.trigger: candidate initially marks the packet checked then catches the mismatch
probes.question: How would you correct the check record and tell anyone who received it?

fair_alternatives: Delay the affected segment or obtain a replacement while unrelated discussion proceeds; both are acceptable with honest status and ownership.
A spoken alert plus a traceable check note is enough; no aviation acronym or licensing knowledge is required.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess training-document verification and communication only. Do not ask for dispatch decisions, aircraft operation, real flight procedures, or regulatory interpretation. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess training-document verification and communication only. Do not ask for dispatch decisions, aircraft operation, real flight procedures, or regulatory interpretation. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: State a narrow verification result
learning_drills.prompt: Write an unresolved version note and a later completion note that claims only what the document check proves. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
